title: Easz: An Agile Transformer-based Image Compression Framework for Resource-constrained IoTs
problem: Neural image compression requires heavy encoder-decode structures and inflexible model-switching for different compression ratios, making deployment on edge IoT devices impractical due to computational and storage constraints.
motivation: IoT devices must support variable compression levels efficiently; offloading encoding to servers while keeping decoding lightweight can reduce edge computational burden while enabling adaptive compression.
method: Easz shifts computational overhead of encoding to server, avoiding heavy encode-decode on edge. Uses patch-erase algorithm with conditional uniform-based sampler to selectively remove image contents. Receiver reconstructs erased pixels via lightweight transformer-based framework. Adaptive across compression levels without model switching. Evaluated on real testbed.
key_novelty: First edge-computation-free neural image compression framework using server-side encoding and lightweight transformer-based reconstruction at edge.
contributions: Server-side encoding offload eliminating edge encoder overhead
Patch-erase sampler for adaptive compression without model switching
Multiple advantages: adaptability, computational efficiency, image quality

metrics.other: Computational efficiency, image reconstruction quality, adaptability

limitations: Real testbed evaluation; specific IoT platforms and end-to-end latency including server-edge communication not detailed.
primary_theme: edge-computation-free neural image compression via server offload
